REVIEW_DECISION: REJECT
RISK_CLASS: high-impact
SUMMARY: The governance prose requires Sol/Opus review for every contract amendment and independent Sol plus Opus approval for token-accounting changes, but the provenance schema and validator enforce reviewer identity only when contract_change_scope is already labeled high_impact. An accepted amendment can therefore carry only an unrelated reviewer, and accounting changes can evade dual approval through misclassification.
FINDING: high|docs/factory-ng/schemas/factory.change-provenance-v1.schema.json|Accepted amendment records require no Sol/Opus reviewer, and no machine-readable affected-domain rule validates high-impact classification|This permits contract activation without the mandatory governance approval and lets token-accounting changes bypass independent Sol and Opus review
REQUIRED_CHANGE: Require accepted amendment records to contain an accepted Sol-or-Opus review; add a required affected-contract-areas field and schema/validator rule classifying token/cost accounting, acceptance semantics, integration authority, and cross-project identity as high_impact with distinct accepted Sol and Opus reviews; add negative fixtures.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: An accepted factory change with contract_change_scope "amendment", reviews containing one accepted Qwen reviewer, and an affected change to warning_reflection_effective_tokens validates under the current schema and provenance validator.
